newsitem.title: USA: Heat wave prompts slight drop in U.S. soy crush.
newsitem.headline: Heat wave prompts slight drop in U.S. soy crush.

text.p: A Midwest heat wave this past week prompted some soybean processors to slightly reduce production as power companies instructed industrial customers to cut electricity use, industry officials said.

U.S. soybean processors used 21.871 million bushels of soybeans this week versus 23.014 million a week ago, according to the National Oilseed Processors Association. Soybean industry sources said power cutbacks because of the heat were responsible for the decline.

Power companies that serve Iowa and portions of Illinois and Minnesota said it was the first time this summer they had instructed corporate customers to reduce power usage. The amount of reduction varied depending on each customer's contract with the power companies.
"Two days ago we did ask our interruptable customers to disconnect from our system the amount they pledged," said Terry Harrmann, spokesman for Interstate Power Co, Dubuque Iowa.
MidAmerican Energy Co, Des Moines, twice this week instructed industrial customers to cut power use.
"We did that on Wednesday... and it is in place today (Friday)," said Kevin Waetke, MidAmerican spokesman.
Cargill Inc said the cutbacks caused slight production changes at its Iowa soybean and corn processing plants.
"It affected us, but not that much," said Peggy Weller, Cargill Inc spokeswoman.
She said the plants either cutback power use or switched to back-up power sources.

Archer Daniels Midland Co said none of its plants were affected because each has "non-interruptable" contracts with the power companies. Plus, each plant produces about 50 percent of its power needs, said Karla Miller, ADM spokeswoman.
